title: queue-depth-sweep-standup-oct06-2026
content:
Queue-depth sweep — standup notes (2026-10-06)
Owners: Elena Ortiz (notes), Marcus Chen (experiments), Priya Rao (observability)
Attendees: Elena, Marcus, Priya, Liam, Sara (joined for TL;DR)
Purpose: Sync on the in-progress queue-depth sweep and microburst/mid-latency spikes seen in last week's shadow runs. Capture quick findings, immediate mitigations, and next experiments.

Background / Why this matters
- Last week's shadow runs on m40k-rt showed intermittent p99 spikes (~900ms -> 1.8s) while p50 stayed ~85ms. Throughput (tokens/s) generally steady, but occasional 2–3x latency bursts caused customer-visible tail latency.
- Hypotheses in flight: a) KV cache thrash during mixed-prefix traffic, b) scheduler allowing too-large effective queue depth combining multiple small requests into a microburst, c) CUDA context/kernel selection jitter for specific seq-len (512) code-path, d) metrics aggregation/agent-induced blocking.

Recent runs summary (10/05–10/06)
- Run IDs: qd-sweep-1025A (control), qd-sweep-1025B (tight max_batch_wait), qd-sweep-1026C (kv-cache pinned), qd-sweep-1026D (disable continuous-batching).
- Setup: 8xA10 nodes, model: rwd-7b-opt, seq-len mix: { prompt: 64 (70%), 256 (20%), 512 (10%) }, client QPS target 120, open-loop traffic replay from prod-sample-aug.
- Observed (high level):
  - qd-sweep-1025A (control): p50=92ms, p95=310ms, p99=1.05s, tokens/s ~45k (stable). Several distinct 1.0–1.8s spikes aligned with sudden small-burst windows.
  - qd-sweep-1025B (max_batch_wait=2ms): p50=98ms, p95=280ms, p99=420ms, tokens/s dropped ~6%. p99 improved significantly — suggests batching wait threshold contributed to combining requests into larger microbursts.
  - qd-sweep-1026C (kv-cache pinned warm): p50=88ms, p95=295ms, p99=600ms. When KV cache warm and pinned in memory between runs, p99 reduced vs control but not as low as 1025B.
  - qd-sweep-1026D (continuous-batching disabled): p50=120ms, p95=370ms, p99=1.2s, tokens/s dropped ~12%. Disabling batching removed some microbursts but hurt median and throughput.
- Interesting: p99 spikes often correlate with a small increase in CPU-side scheduling (ksoftirq) and sudden growth in host-level memcpy spikes. Sequence-length 512 requests disproportionately present in windows preceding spikes.

Initial interpretations / working hypotheses
1) Scheduler/batching timing: The default max_batch_wait (5ms) occasionally lets a flurry of small short requests queue up and be combined into a larger GPU dispatch; combined with warmup overhead we see long tail latency. Tightening max_batch_wait to 2ms reduced p99 but slightly lowered throughput. Tradeoff looks promising for tail-sensitive SLAs.
2) KV cache temperature: Cold or partially-evicted KV entries for longer sequences can cause extra memory churn (host->device transfers) at dispatch boundaries — contributes to tail events but not dominant. Pinning KV improved some runs.
3) Kernel jitter for seq-len 512: Some kernel variants run slower; if the runtime selects a slower kernel path under certain memory alignment or tensor shapes, that can explain isolated high latencies. Need kernel-level profiling.
4) Host-side stalls (memcpy/PCIe bursts): Observed memcpy bursts on the host just before p99 spikes. Could be concurrent background tasks (snapshotting, metrics egress) or GC-like behavior in the agent.

Immediate actions (next 72h)
- Marcus: Run targeted kernel-profile traces for seq-len 512 using nvprof/nsys on qd-sweep-1025A replica and attach flame graphs. Ticket: RI-3571. Due: 2026-10-08.
- Priya: Add temporary agent-level EGRESS throttling on a subset of nodes and rerun control to check if memcpy bursts disappear. Capture perf counters for PCIe and host memcpy. Due: 2026-10-08.
- Elena + Liam: Run a latency-first shadow with max_batch_wait=1ms and tuned batch size cap (max_batch_size=24) to see p99 impact and throughput delta. Keep a separate run with adaptive batching (heuristic learned from shadow). Due: 2026-10-09.
- Sara: Create minimal reproducer (short script) that sends concentrated 512-seq requests to reproduce the spike locally on dev cluster. Link here when ready. Due: 2026-10-07.

Experiment plan (rough)
- Phase A (isolate scheduling): runs with max_batch_wait {1ms,2ms,5ms,10ms} × max_batch_size {16,32}. Measure p50/p95/p99, tokens/s, GPU utilization, host memcpy.
- Phase B (kv-cache): warm vs cold (warm pinned / evict between runs) × same qdw set.
- Phase C (agent noise): run with metrics egress off, snapshot disabled, and with a lightweight egress to replicate production.
- Phase D (kernel): kernel traces + try forced kernel variant selection (if available) for seq-len 512 on one shard.

Notes / informal observations
- We saw one outlier where p99 hit 2.4s when a maintenance snapshot job coincided with an automated scaling event — need safer scheduling for background ops.
- Disabling continuous-batching felt like harming median but reduced some spike patterns; suggests we need smarter heuristics (adaptive thresholds) rather than an on/off knob.
- No evidence that GC of Python agents is the root cause, but cannot rule out intermittent host processes.

Open questions / unresolved
- Can we make the batching heuristic latency-aware instead of purely time-based? (e.g., if seq-len distribution shows more 512s, prefer smaller batch sizes)
- Is kernel selection non-deterministic across runs? If yes, can we record the selected kernel id in telemetry for postmortem correlation?
- Should Dedicated customers have a different default max_batch_wait to favor tails? Need product input.

References / logs
- Shadow runs stored in s3://redwood-bench/qd-sweep/2026-10-05/*. Please check run metadata: run_id and experiment tags there.
- Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4821 (adds max_batch_wait param to runtime config)
- Jira: RI-3571 (kernel-profile for seq-len 512)
- Confluence notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/PerfQueueSweep2026 (experiment tracker)

Action item recap
- Marcus: kernel profiling (RI-3571) — due 10/08
- Priya: agent egress throttle test + PCIe counters — due 10/08
- Elena & Liam: tight max_batch_wait shadow (1ms) + adaptive batch run — due 10/09
- Sara: local reproducer for 512-heavy bursts — due 10/07
- Product: decide whether to trial lower default max_batch_wait for dedicated tiers (ask PM in next sync)

Next sync
- Quick async updates in #infra-perf; full follow-up standup Fri 2026-10-09 09:30 PDT (20 min).

Notes to self (todo / ideas)
- Add a telemetry metric: chosen_batch_width and chosen_batch_latency_estimate to correlate with tail events.
- Consider small A/B with real traffic (1% RTP) to validate tradeoffs in production conditions.
- If kernel trace shows branching on tensor alignment, try changing pad strategy for 512 sequences.

---
End of standup notes.
